entities.name: Mao Zedong
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Mao Zedong (1893–1976) was the founding chairman of the People's Republic of China whose revolutionary vision reshaped the most populous nation on Earth. A peasant's son from Hunan province, he merged Marxism-Leninism with Chinese agrarian revolution to create 'Maoism.'

He led the Chinese Communist Party through the Long March (1934–35), the war against Japan, and civil war against Chiang Kai-shek's Nationalists, proclaiming the People's Republic on October 1, 1949. His rule brought land reform and literacy campaigns but also catastrophic failures: the Great Leap Forward (1958–62) caused a famine killing 15–55 million people.

The Cultural Revolution (1966–76) unleashed Red Guards against 'bourgeois elements,' devastating China's intellectual and cultural life. Yet Mao also normalized relations with the US (Nixon's 1972 visit) and remains a deeply complex figure — revered as China's liberator, condemned for its worst peacetime catastrophe.

effects: Founding of People's Republic of China (1949)
